lines: Namaste, I'm Hema. You're watching This Day, That Year.
Today's date is the fifth of October. And fifteen years ago, it was 2026.
Old sport. India finished fourth at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with eighty five medals, including gold in hockey and cricket.
Today the medals are leased by the hour, and the podium has a surge price.
Old fuel. Brent crude stayed above one hundred dollars a barrel, yet petrol in Mumbai held steady at one hundred eleven rupees.
Vintage gadget: the petrol pump. In 2041, we refuel with patience, and the queue is the fuel.
Old markets. Foreign investors sold Indian shares in September, the biggest monthly outflow in six months. Today, money leaves by itself and sends a postcard.
That's the record. Everything else is just a take. I'm Hema. Namaste, see you at the next bulletin.
Namaskara! Meter down. Tchu Tchu reporting, live from the taxi.
A passenger says petrol is steady even though oil is above a hundred dollars. I said my meter is also steady: it only goes up. Work is warship.
India got eighty five medals at the Asian Games. The Dalmatian wants one for sitting still. Something is fishy with the Dalmatian.
Eighth notice from Fa King Construction at Celeb Shauchalay. Now scented with lavender. Who notices a notice?
Tchu Tchu, AIMTV, Bombai. The meter is still running.
Hi guys! It's Stomach Challo, and today I have left the country again. Passport not needed, only comfortable shoes. I love foreign.
Okay, it is Matheran. But no cars are allowed here, which is so Swiss. Zermatt wishes it had this much mud.
I took a horse to the viewpoint. The horse took the selfie. Very professional, very international.
The red mud sticks to everything. My shoes now have a red carpet, and they have not even been invited anywhere.
The monkeys here run a tight security desk. Snacks must be declared. Very airport.
That's it for today. Stay hungry, stay foreign. This is Stomach Challo, signing off from West India.
Namaste, Juhu Chaiwala here. Welcome to Tomorrow Shop. Products from the future, delivered to the footpath.
Today's product is the Bull Pillow. A cushion that gets softer when the market falls, so you always land gently.
Fifteen years ago the market fell for eight weeks straight. We did not fix it. We made a pillow.
At the sunny entrance, the Bull Pillow costs Rs 9,000. At the shadow entrance, it costs Rs 120. Same pillow. Different sky.
It comes with a free tip printed on the label: buy low. Nobody has ever followed it.
You can pay in chai. Chai is Rs 12 at the shadow entrance and Rs 900 at the sunny entrance, so the exchange rate depends on where you stand.
Here is your chai. From a bot.
Are you tired of sleeping through your own life? Try Fa Wake Up, the alarm clock that rings your relatives.
One ring and your aunt asks why you are not married. Another and she asks why you are still awake.
Fa Wake Up costs only Rs 499 a month. Side effects may include early mornings, loud cousins and eviction.
Fa Corp. We wake what you sleep on.
Namaste. Sindhi Crawford here, Road Cross, since two thousand eight. The monsoon is leaving, but the puddles are not.
Hot and humid means slow walkers and quick drivers. Look both ways, then look again. A zebra crossing is a suggestion only if you are a zebra.
Don't take tension. We help you cross.
Baa baa. Today's blessing: may your chai be warm, your queue be short, and your notice be unread.
